authorization: User explicitly requested original reference UI, no in-App exit during recording, and interrupted recording recovery. No quota/payment/relationship/notification eligibility changes authorized or made.
causes: Old recording treated any blur/non-active AppState as a terminal interruption, destroyed the recorder, and returned the parent to idle without a partial checkpoint.
Null completion and local draft-write failures also returned to idle; recording completion, valid content, durable save, and server acknowledgement were conflated in the UI.
Recording and preview used a growing centered ScrollView and different toy sizes instead of the supplied fixed-stage layout.

Input could use a stale/uninitialized frame clock, ignored movement could start the input clock, and gesture finalization could cancel rendered fingers without closing recorder pointers. These paths now have counterexample tests. They are not claimed to be the sole cause of every historical interruption.
clientChanges: Intro is a cream overlay; acknowledging it goes directly to first-touch-armed recording, without an extra Record 60 seconds page.

Brown instruction header, upper heart counter/outline timer, fixed toy size and baseline, bottom Squeeze/Bonk. At completion only the bottom main action changes to cream Send The Love Bomb. Record again is a header action.

Recording uses one logical foreground-time axis, pauses on background/blur, and rebases on resume. Partial and completed checkpoints survive process restart in existing encrypted, managed account-scoped storage.
Navigation guards are scoped to a started, live recording and released on completion, revocation or unavailable required content; allowance changes cannot unmount a still-locked recorder.

Every partial write captures actor/partner/pair scope. Restored UI pins the original toy/photo IDs; stale callbacks cannot save or enqueue old content under a new scope. Input batches also carry a foreground generation so queued pre-pause input cannot reopen held pointers after resume, even if React batches inactive/active without rendering.
Approximate 500ms coalesced checkpoints, lifecycle flush, closed-pointer restoration without invented counts; excess event sampling is bounded without discarding the whole minute.

A completed clip is retained on local write failure. Zero completed actions produce an explicit non-sendable completed state with a re-record exit. Only acknowledged sends display the success overlay.

Absolute controls are inside a full-height interaction container rather than relying on out-of-bounds native hit testing. Ordinary toy layout is unchanged unless these optional presentation props are supplied.

recordingPerformance.scope: UI-frame callback during the 21-touch full-minute layout candidate before the final queued-input-generation-only guard; excludes cold open before first touch and first frame after foreground. Not an independent compositor/GPU trace. No concurrent build or large test suite during sampling.
recordingPerformance.assessment: Typical recording sustained the frame budget; one slow interval remains. Not zero drops or an all-device guarantee. Prior cold-open limits from the original feature report are not waived.

finalForegroundRecoveryPerformance.scope: Final hashed bundle, real recording after two physical button actions and a foreground/background cycle. Same UI-frame-callback limitations. No concurrent compilation or large test suite; this single sample does not erase the earlier 56ms slow interval or prove all devices/cold opens.

recoveryLimits: The App cannot forbid OS backgrounding, force termination, power loss or uninstall. It pauses and restores the latest successfully written checkpoint.
A force kill can lose approximately one coalesced save interval under normal load; suspension, blocked JS or storage failure can increase this. Do not promise zero loss.
Recovery occurs when re-entering the recording destination, without adding startup navigation that overrides existing launch priorities.
Old recordings already discarded by the previous implementation cannot be reconstructed.
Identity/relationship revocation still clears or rejects old content; recording locks cannot override security.
